terms.gloss: a ball, a sphere, a globe
evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.47: ex solidīs globus, which Cicero says is how he chooses to render Greek σφαῖρα
Cic. Rep. 6.15: ille globus, quae terra dīcitur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The Latin word for the solid, which Cicero sets beside circulus for the plane figure: “so I choose to render σφαῖρα”. A ball to play with is pila (see “ball”); a model of the earth globus terrārum (see “globe”).

terms.gloss: a sphere; a ball; a model of the heavens
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.65: sphaerae figūra et cylindrī
terms.comment: The Greek word, which Cicero also uses; Lewis & Short calls globus its pure Latin.

phrases.latin: Pila globus est, nōn circulus: circulus in chartā pingitur, globus manū tenētur.
phrases.english: A ball is a sphere, not a circle: a circle is drawn on paper, a sphere is held in the hand.

phrases.latin: cōnum tibi ais et cylindrum et pȳramidem pulchriōrem quam sphaeram vidērī
phrases.english: you say the cone and the cylinder and the pyramid seem to you more beautiful than the sphere

phrases.latin: animum advertī columellam nōn multum ē dūmīs ēminentem, in quā inerat sphaerae figūra et cylindrī
phrases.english: I noticed a little column standing not far out of the brambles, on which there was the figure of a sphere and a cylinder

sources: Lewis & Short: globus · Lewis & Short: sphaera
